audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Isaac sending Jacob to Paddan-Aram, blessing of Abraham, Esau's additional marriage, Jacob's ladder/stairway dream, Bethel naming, stone pillar, and vow/tithe language.

verses.restored: Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, commanded him, and said to him, You shall not take a woman from the daughters of Canaan.

familiar.text: And Isaac called Jacob, and blessed him, and charged him...

modern.text: So Isaac called for Jacob and blessed him. “Do not take a wife from the Canaanite women,” he commanded.

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֥א יִצְחָ֛ק אֶֽל יַעֲקֹ֖ב וַיְבָ֣רֶךְ אֹת֑וֹ וַיְצַוֵּ֨הוּ֙ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ל֔וֹ לֹֽא תִקַּ֥ח אִשָּׁ֖ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן

verses.restored: Rise, go to Paddan-Aram, to the house of Bethuel your mother’s father, and take for yourself from there a woman from the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.

familiar.text: Arise, go to Padanaram, to the house of Bethuel thy mother's father...

modern.text: “Go at once to Paddan-aram, to the house of your mother’s father Bethuel, and take a wife from among the daughters of Laban, your mother’s brother.

original.text: ק֥וּם לֵךְ֙ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֔ם בֵּ֥יתָה בְתוּאֵ֖ל אֲבִ֣י אִמֶּ֑ךָ וְקַח לְךָ֤ מִשָּׁם֙ אִשָּׁ֔ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת לָבָ֖ן אֲחִ֥י אִמֶּֽךָ

verses.restored: May El Shaddai bless you, make you fruitful, and multiply you, so that you become an assembly of peoples.

familiar.text: And God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful...

notes.title: El Shaddai
notes.body: Isaac invokes the covenant title associated with Abraham’s renaming and fruitfulness.

modern.text: May God Almighty bless you and make you fruitful and multiply you, so that you may become a company of peoples.

original.text: וְאֵ֤ל שַׁדַּי֙ יְבָרֵ֣ךְ אֹֽתְךָ֔ וְיַפְרְךָ֖ וְיַרְבֶּ֑ךָ וְהָיִ֖יתָ לִקְהַ֥ל עַמִּֽים

verses.restored: May he give you the blessing of Abraham, to you and to your seed with you, so that you may possess the land of your sojournings, which the Divine gave to Abraham.

familiar.text: And give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed...

notes.title: Blessing of Abraham
notes.body: The covenant blessing is now explicitly passed to Jacob.

modern.text: And may He give the blessing of Abraham to you and your descendants, so that you may possess the land where you dwell as a foreigner, the land God gave to Abraham.”

original.text: וְיִֽתֶּן לְךָ֙ אֶת בִּרְכַּ֣ת אַבְרָהָ֔ם לְךָ֖ וּלְזַרְעֲךָ֣ אִתָּ֑ךְ לְרִשְׁתְּךָ֙ אֶת אֶ֣רֶץ מְגֻרֶ֔יךָ אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥ן אֱלֹהִ֖ים לְאַבְרָהָֽם

verses.restored: Isaac sent Jacob away, and he went to Paddan-Aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean, brother of Rebekah, mother of Jacob and Esau.

familiar.text: And Isaac sent away Jacob: and he went to Padanaram unto Laban...

modern.text: So Isaac sent Jacob to Paddan-aram, to Laban son of Bethuel the Aramean, the brother of Rebekah, who was the mother of Jacob and Esau. Esau Marries Mahalath

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֤ח יִצְחָק֙ אֶֽת יַעֲקֹ֔ב וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֑ם אֶל לָבָ֤ן בֶּן בְּתוּאֵל֙ הָֽאֲרַמִּ֔י אֲחִ֣י רִבְקָ֔ה אֵ֥ם יַעֲקֹ֖ב וְעֵשָֽׂו

verses.restored: Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-Aram to take a woman from there, and that as he blessed him he commanded him, saying, You shall not take a woman from the daughters of Canaan,

familiar.text: When Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob...

modern.text: Now Esau learned that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him to Paddan-aram to take a wife there, commanding him, “Do not marry a Canaanite woman,”

original.text: וַיַּ֣רְא עֵשָׂ֗ו כִּֽי בֵרַ֣ךְ יִצְחָק֮ אֶֽת יַעֲקֹב֒ וְשִׁלַּ֤ח אֹתוֹ֙ פַּדֶּ֣נָֽה אֲרָ֔ם לָקַֽחַת ל֥וֹ מִשָּׁ֖ם אִשָּׁ֑ה בְּבָרֲכ֣וֹ אֹת֔וֹ וַיְצַ֤ו עָלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹֽא תִקַּ֥ח אִשָּׁ֖ה מִבְּנ֥וֹת כְּנָֽעַן

verses.restored: and that Jacob had listened to his father and his mother and had gone to Paddan-Aram,

familiar.text: And that Jacob obeyed his father and his mother...

modern.text: and that Jacob had obeyed his father and mother and gone to Paddan-aram.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע יַעֲקֹ֔ב אֶל אָבִ֖יו וְאֶל אִמּ֑וֹ וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ פַּדֶּ֥נָֽה אֲרָֽם

verses.restored: Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan were harmful in the eyes of Isaac his father.

familiar.text: And Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father;

modern.text: And seeing that his father Isaac disapproved of the Canaanite women,

original.text: וַיַּ֣רְא עֵשָׂ֔ו כִּ֥י רָע֖וֹת בְּנ֣וֹת כְּנָ֑עַן בְּעֵינֵ֖י יִצְחָ֥ק אָבִֽיו

verses.restored: So Esau went to Ishmael and took Mahalath, daughter of Ishmael son of Abraham, sister of Nebaioth, in addition to his women, to be his woman.

familiar.text: Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath...

notes.title: Esau responds by marriage
notes.body: Esau tries to address his parents’ displeasure by marrying within Abraham’s wider family through Ishmael.

modern.text: Esau went to Ishmael and married Mahalath, the sister of Nebaioth and daughter of Abraham’s son Ishmael, in addition to the wives he already had. Jacob’s Ladder

original.text: וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ עֵשָׂ֖ו אֶל יִשְׁמָעֵ֑אל וַיִּקַּ֡ח אֶֽת מָחֲלַ֣ת בַּת יִשְׁמָעֵ֨אל בֶּן אַבְרָהָ֜ם אֲח֧וֹת נְבָי֛וֹת עַל נָשָׁ֖יו ל֥וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: Jacob went out from Beersheba and went toward Haran.

familiar.text: And Jacob went out from Beersheba, and went toward Haran.

modern.text: Meanwhile Jacob left Beersheba and set out for Haran.

original.text: וַיֵּצֵ֥א יַעֲקֹ֖ב מִבְּאֵ֣ר שָׁ֑בַע וַיֵּ֖לֶךְ חָרָֽנָה

verses.restored: He came upon a place and spent the night there, because the sun had gone down. He took one of the stones of the place, set it at his head, and lay down in that place.

familiar.text: And he lighted upon a certain place, and tarried there all night...

notes.title: The place
notes.body: Maqom, place, repeats and becomes sacred through encounter.

modern.text: On reaching a certain place, he spent the night there because the sun had set. And taking one of the stones from that place, he put it under his head and lay down to sleep.

original.text: וַיִּפְגַּ֨ע בַּמָּק֜וֹם וַיָּ֤לֶן שָׁם֙ כִּי בָ֣א הַשֶּׁ֔מֶשׁ וַיִּקַּח֙ מֵאַבְנֵ֣י הַמָּק֔וֹם וַיָּ֖שֶׂם מְרַֽאֲשֹׁתָ֑יו וַיִּשְׁכַּ֖ב בַּמָּק֥וֹם הַהֽוּא

verses.restored: He dreamed, and look, a stairway was set on the earth, its head reaching the heavens, and look, messengers of the Divine were ascending and descending on it.

familiar.text: And he dreamed, and behold a ladder set up on the earth...

notes.title: Stairway/ladder
notes.body: Sullam may be ladder, stairway, or ramp. It joins earth and heavens in Jacob’s dream.

modern.text: And Jacob had a dream about a ladder that rested on the earth with its top reaching up to heaven, and God’s angels were going up and down the ladder.

original.text: וַֽיַּחֲלֹ֗ם וְהִנֵּ֤ה סֻלָּם֙ מֻצָּ֣ב אַ֔רְצָה וְרֹאשׁ֖וֹ מַגִּ֣יעַ הַשָּׁמָ֑יְמָה וְהִנֵּה֙ מַלְאֲכֵ֣י אֱלֹהִ֔ים עֹלִ֥ים וְיֹרְדִ֖ים בּֽוֹ

verses.restored: And look, the Eternal stood above it and said, I am the Eternal, Divine of Abraham your father and Divine of Isaac. The land on which you are lying, to you I will give it and to your seed.

familiar.text: And, behold, the LORD stood above it, and said...

modern.text: And there at the top the LORD was standing and saying, “I am the LORD, the God of your father Abraham and the God of Isaac. I will give you and your descendants the land on which you now lie.

original.text: וְהִנֵּ֨ה יְהוָ֜ה נִצָּ֣ב עָלָיו֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ אֲנִ֣י יְהוָ֗ה אֱלֹהֵי֙ אַבְרָהָ֣ם אָבִ֔יךָ וֵאלֹהֵ֖י יִצְחָ֑ק הָאָ֗רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֤ר אַתָּה֙ שֹׁכֵ֣ב עָלֶ֔יהָ לְךָ֥ אֶתְּנֶ֖נָּה וּלְזַרְעֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Your seed shall be like the dust of the earth. You shall spread westward, eastward, northward, and southward, and in you and in your seed all the families of the ground shall be blessed.

familiar.text: And thy seed shall be as the dust of the earth...

modern.text: Your descendants will be like the dust of the earth, and you will spread out to the west and east and north and south. All the families of the earth will be blessed through you and your offspring.

original.text: וְהָיָ֤ה זַרְעֲךָ֙ כַּעֲפַ֣ר הָאָ֔רֶץ וּפָרַצְתָּ֛ יָ֥מָּה וָקֵ֖דְמָה וְצָפֹ֣נָה וָנֶ֑גְבָּה וְנִבְרֲכ֥וּ בְךָ֛ כָּל מִשְׁפְּחֹ֥ת הָאֲדָמָ֖ה וּבְזַרְעֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Look, I am with you, and I will keep you wherever you go. I will return you to this ground, for I will not leave you until I have done what I have spoken to you.

familiar.text: And, behold, I am with thee, and will keep thee in all places...

notes.title: I am with you
notes.body: The promise centers presence, protection, return, and completion.

modern.text: Look, I am with you, and I will watch over you wherever you go, and I will bring you back to this land. For I will not leave you until I have done what I have promised you.”

original.text: וְהִנֵּ֨ה אָנֹכִ֜י עִמָּ֗ךְ וּשְׁמַרְתִּ֨יךָ֙ בְּכֹ֣ל אֲשֶׁר תֵּלֵ֔ךְ וַהֲשִׁ֣בֹתִ֔יךָ אֶל הָאֲדָמָ֖ה הַזֹּ֑את כִּ֚י לֹ֣א אֶֽעֱזָבְךָ֔ עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִם עָשִׂ֔יתִי אֵ֥ת אֲשֶׁר דִּבַּ֖רְתִּי לָֽךְ

verses.restored: Jacob awoke from his sleep and said, Surely the Eternal is in this place, and I did not know.

familiar.text: And Jacob awaked out of his sleep, and he said, Surely the LORD is in this place...

modern.text: When Jacob woke up, he thought, “Surely the LORD is in this place, and I was unaware of it.”

original.text: וַיִּיקַ֣ץ יַעֲקֹב֮ מִשְּׁנָתוֹ֒ וַיֹּ֕אמֶר אָכֵן֙ יֵ֣שׁ יְהוָ֔ה בַּמָּק֖וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה וְאָנֹכִ֖י לֹ֥א יָדָֽעְתִּי

verses.restored: He was afraid and said, How awe-filled is this place! This is none other than the house of the Divine, and this is the gate of the heavens.

familiar.text: And he was afraid, and said, How dreadful is this place!...

notes.title: Awe-filled
notes.body: Nora can mean fearful, awesome, or awe-filled. The fear is sacred awe.

modern.text: And he was afraid and said, “How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God; this is the gate of heaven!” The Stone of Bethel

original.text: וַיִּירָא֙ וַיֹּאמַ֔ר מַה נּוֹרָ֖א הַמָּק֣וֹם הַזֶּ֑ה אֵ֣ין זֶ֗ה כִּ֚י אִם בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְזֶ֖ה שַׁ֥עַר הַשָּׁמָֽיִם

verses.restored: Jacob rose early in the morning, took the stone that he had set at his head, set it up as a pillar, and poured oil on its head.

familiar.text: And Jacob rose up early in the morning, and took the stone...

modern.text: Early the next morning, Jacob took the stone that he had placed under his head, and he set it up as a pillar. He poured oil on top of it,

original.text: וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֨ם יַעֲקֹ֜ב בַּבֹּ֗קֶר וַיִּקַּ֤ח אֶת הָאֶ֨בֶן֙ אֲשֶׁר שָׂ֣ם מְרַֽאֲשֹׁתָ֔יו וַיָּ֥שֶׂם אֹתָ֖הּ מַצֵּבָ֑ה וַיִּצֹ֥ק שֶׁ֖מֶן עַל רֹאשָֽׁהּ

verses.restored: He called the name of that place Bethel, though Luz was the name of the city at first.

familiar.text: And he called the name of that place Bethel...

notes.title: Bethel
notes.body: Bethel means House of God/the Divine.

modern.text: and he called that place Bethel, though previously the city had been named Luz.

original.text: וַיִּקְרָ֛א אֶת שֵֽׁם הַמָּק֥וֹם הַה֖וּא בֵּֽית אֵ֑ל וְאוּלָ֛ם ל֥וּז שֵׁם הָעִ֖יר לָרִאשֹׁנָֽה

verses.restored: Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If the Divine will be with me, keep me on this way that I am going, give me bread to eat and clothing to wear,

familiar.text: And Jacob vowed a vow, saying, If God will be with me...

notes.title: Jacob’s vow
notes.body: Jacob responds conditionally to the unconditional promise, asking for presence, protection, bread, clothing, and return.

modern.text: Then Jacob made a vow, saying, “If God will be with me and watch over me on this journey, and if He will provide me with food to eat and clothes to wear,

original.text: וַיִּדַּ֥ר יַעֲקֹ֖ב נֶ֣דֶר לֵאמֹ֑ר אִם יִהְיֶ֨ה אֱלֹהִ֜ים עִמָּדִ֗י וּשְׁמָרַ֨נִי֙ בַּדֶּ֤רֶךְ הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָנֹכִ֣י הוֹלֵ֔ךְ וְנָֽתַן לִ֥י לֶ֛חֶם לֶאֱכֹ֖ל וּבֶ֥גֶד לִלְבֹּֽשׁ

verses.restored: and I return in peace to my father’s house, then the Eternal shall be my Divine.

familiar.text: So that I come again to my father's house in peace; then shall the LORD be my God:

modern.text: so that I may return safely to my father’s house, then the LORD will be my God.

original.text: וְשַׁבְתִּ֥י בְשָׁל֖וֹם אֶל בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֑י וְהָיָ֧ה יְהוָ֛ה לִ֖י לֵאלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: This stone that I have set up as a pillar shall be the house of the Divine, and of all that you give me I will surely give a tenth to you.

familiar.text: And this stone, which I have set for a pillar, shall be God's house...

modern.text: And this stone I have set up as a pillar will be God’s house, and of all that You give me I will surely give You a tenth.”

original.text: וְהָאֶ֣בֶן הַזֹּ֗את אֲשֶׁר שַׂ֨מְתִּי֙ מַצֵּבָ֔ה יִהְיֶ֖ה בֵּ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֑ים וְכֹל֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר תִּתֶּן לִ֔י עַשֵּׂ֖ר אֲעַשְּׂרֶ֥נּוּ לָֽךְ
